SM.farout.{u_1} (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] [Invertible 2] (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
  (∀ (D H : SM.TripleArray n R),
      (∃ Ψ,
          (∀ (Y : SM.IntervalArray n R),
              (SM.nearFarTransform D H fun I => (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (RingHom.id R) Y) (Ψ I)) = Y) ∧
            ∀ (X : SM.IntervalArray n R),
              (fun I => (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (RingHom.id R) (SM.nearFarTransform D H X)) (Ψ I)) = X) ∧
        SM.nearFarTransform D H = SM.farTransform H ∘ SM.nearTransform D) ∧
    (∀ (P : SM.LabelledTuple n) (hP : SM.G1 P) (g : ZMod n),
        (SM.nearFarTransform (SM.geometricBoundaryArray P g) (SM.geometricBoundaryArray P g) fun I =>
              ↑(SM.openTreeSum P hP g I)) =
            SM.boundaryUnitArray ∧
          ↑(SM.treeCoefficient P hP g hn) =
              SM.nearFarTransform (SM.geometricBoundaryArray P g) (-SM.geometricBoundaryArray P g)
                (fun I => ↑(SM.openTreeSum P hP g I)) (SM.fullBoundaryInterval hn) ∧
            ↑(SM.treeCoefficient P hP g hn) =
              SM.farOnlyOutput (SM.geometricBoundaryArray P g) (SM.fullBoundaryInterval hn)) ∧
      (∀ (D₁ D₂ H : SM.TripleArray n R) (X₁ X₂ : SM.IntervalArray n R),
          SM.nearFarTransform D₁ H X₁ = SM.boundaryUnitArray →
            SM.nearFarTransform D₂ H X₂ = SM.boundaryUnitArray →
              SM.nearFarTransform D₁ (-H) X₁ = SM.nearFarTransform D₂ (-H) X₂) ∧
        (∀ (H : SM.TripleArray n R) (J : SM.BoundaryInterval n),
            (2 ≤ J.leaves → SM.farTransform H (SM.farOnlyCoordinates H) J = 0) ∧
              (J.leaves = 1 → SM.farTransform H (SM.farOnlyCoordinates H) J = 1 ∧ SM.farOnlyOutput H J = 1)) ∧
          ∀ (P : SM.LabelledTuple n) (g : ZMod n) (J : SM.BoundaryInterval n) (hJ : 2 ≤ J.leaves)
            (hP : SM.G1 (SM.restrictedWordTuple P g J)),
            SM.edge (SM.restrictedWordTuple P g J) 0 = SM.boundaryWord P g J.left - SM.boundaryWord P g J.right ∧
              SM.farOnlyOutput (SM.geometricBoundaryArray P g) J =
                ↑(SM.treeCoefficient (SM.restrictedWordTuple P g J) hP 0 ⋯)

mathematical_justification.clause: Actual unmarked fine cuts and all inner cuts
mathematical_justification.assessment: RefinementUnmarked is every fine interior index whose actual physical position is absent from the outer cut set. Each inner interior cut lies strictly inside its outer part, lies in the global refined cut set by restriction, and cannot be an outer cut because the part is consecutive. The actual fine index is recovered by the physical-position equivalence. Equality of images forces equality of strict outer-part interiors and then inner indices. Conversely an unmarked fine cut lies in a half-open outer part; it cannot equal that part’s left endpoint because that would be an outer cut, so it is strictly interior and occurs in the exact recovered inner composition. Thus all and only unmarked cuts occur once, including empty unary domains.

mathematical_justification.clause: Exact inner neighboring triples
mathematical_justification.assessment: For each inner cut, the preceding and following child intervals are globally consecutive in the refined cut set. The existing consecutive-triple uniqueness theorem therefore identifies both neighbors around the same physical middle cut. inner_nearTriple_transport proves equality of the full triples, not merely equality of their signs or scalar samples. Applying any triple-valued factor function and reindexing the full sigma of inner interior indices gives the exact unmarked fine product. The independent entry consumer checks all three positions explicitly.

mathematical_justification.clause: All marked cuts and global far endpoints
mathematical_justification.assessment: Every outer interior position remains a refined interior position by cut-set containment. The position-preserving outer-index map is injective; any marked fine interior position is an actual outer cut strictly between the global endpoints, so it has a unique outer interior index. RefinementMarked therefore contains exactly these positions. Both farTriple constructions use the same source interval I; their lower and upper entries are I.left and I.right, and their middle entries agree by the position lemma. The independent consumer checks those exact global endpoints, excluding an accidental inner-interval far sample. Reindexing arbitrary far-triple factors supplies precisely every marked factor.

mathematical_justification.clause: Exact partition and half coefficients
mathematical_justification.assessment: refinementMarks stores the actual outer interior positions as marks of the fine composition. refinementMarkIndices recovers their fine indices; membership is equivalent to membership in the outer cut set because all fine indices already exclude global endpoints. Subtype products therefore equal products over this exact finite marked set and its complementary interior-index set. The independent factor-count consumer combines both index equivalences and the subtype-complement cardinality formula to show that the outer interior count plus every inner interior count equals the fine interior count. Thus every refined interior cut supplies exactly one half factor. Near-only weights become D of the actual neighboring triple times inverse two; far-only weights become negative H of the global-endpoint triple times inverse two.

mathematical_justification.clause: Complete recovered and arbitrary raw nested summands

The proved near-factor product, marked far-factor product and full refined child-coordinate product then yield exactly the source marked/unmarked coefficient times the complete refined child product. The ring is arbitrary CommRing with invertible two; no field, ordering or nontriviality premise appears. Independent raw-family consumers replace every recovered inner composition by the original arbitrary family using refinementInner_flatten and whole-family congruence, so coverage does not depend on a restricted reconstructed-family presentation. Unary outer data gives no marks; an identical outer/fine cut set marks every fine position; every unary inner coefficient is one.
